notes: DEAD: "repeat_video" has zero usages anywhere in the app and is not even present in the app's own English source (assets/l10n/en.yaml). Nothing in the app can ever render it. Safe to remove.

PRODUCT DECISION: "repeat_first_meditation_title" exists in the app's English source but no screen reads it. The repeat-user path (lib/presentation/screens/meditation/meditation_intent/meditation_intent_screen.dart, _resolveFirstMeditationCardCopy) deliberately reuses first_meditation_title and only swaps in repeat_first_meditation_subtitle. Either wire it up or drop it — kept in `order` under the trailing unused section for now.

VARIANT SETS a translator must understand: (1) time of day — title_today vs title_tonight; quick_{morning,afternoon,evening}_{title,subtitle}; locked_quick_start_description_{morning,afternoon,evening}. Exactly one of each set shows, chosen by the clock. (2) experience level — first_meditation_subtitle vs repeat_first_meditation_subtitle, and ready_to_try_subtitle_beginner vs ready_to_try_subtitle_repeat. The 'beginner' variant shows for users who answered that they are completely new (and for anyone who skipped the question); the 'repeat' variant for everyone else.
LINE BREAKS to preserve in the English: title_today, title_tonight and quick_afternoon_subtitle each contain a deliberate line break.

This leaf spans four surfaces, not one screen: the choose-your-meditation screen (Step 1 of 3), the locked-card pop-up, the onboarding welcome slides, and the explainer video. Sections are ordered surface by surface, each surface top-to-bottom.

Reordered relative to the current schema: the quick-meditation titles and subtitles are now paired per time of day (morning title, morning subtitle, afternoon title, …) instead of all titles then all subtitles, so each mutually-exclusive variant reads as one unit.
personalized_title does double duty: it is both the personalised card title and the heading of the locked personalised pop-up. Kept once, in the card section.

description: The optional foot-soak step, offered as the last setup screen just before the meditation starts.

order.description: Step indicator in the header at the very top, e.g. "Step 3 of 3".
The question in large text at the top of the screen, asking whether the user wants to soak their feet.
Link with a play icon just below the photo, opening a short how-to video.
Main button at the bottom — starts the meditation with a foot soak.
Second button at the bottom — starts the meditation without a foot soak.

The short sentence encouraging the user to soak their feet. On screen it sits directly under the title and above the photo — near the top of the screen, not at the bottom where this field appears here. It is formatted text because one word in it is emphasised; keep that emphasis.

notes: The key was given as "description [richText]"; the stored slug is "description" (confirmed in translationsSchema.json) and the "[richText]" part is only the type annotation, so it is emitted as "description".

In the app's English source this one sentence is still three separate strings (description_prefix / description_emphasis / description_suffix) so the middle word can be bold-italic. The CMS models it as a single formatted-text field — its description tells the translator to keep the emphasis rather than exposing the split.
The formatted-text field renders after the plain string fields in the editor, so its description explicitly states that the text really sits between the title and the photo.
